To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DsbA is a peculiar substrate of the Sec system and that the SecY protein is a key component of the export machinery.

(i) DsbA export depends on the translocon but not on the signal recognition particle and SecB, (ii) the precursor of DsbA folds into a protease resistant structure in the cytoplasm and is exported as such, (iii) export of DsbA is not posttranslational, and (iv) DsbA is exported through a special route in the translocon
DsbA export is SecA and Ffh dependent but SecB independent and that SecY mutants that impair translocation of most preproteins have only a minor effect on DsbA translocation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the peculiarities of the DsbA transport across the cytoplasmic membranes of Escherichia coil and the role of the translocon in this process.

the peculiar properties of the DsbA translocation, which is not only a model for the study of protein export across the cytoplasmic membranes of Gram-negative bacteria but may also serve as an experimental system for the investigation of the mechanism of translocation of the periplasmically localized proteins.
the export of a periplasmically acting protein and its implications in the understanding of the translocon function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DsbA export is SecA dependent but SecB and signal recognition particle independent, that the SecY periplasmic loop is involved in the export process, and that DsbA is translocated by a mechanism different from that of the general secretory pathway.
DsbA export depends on SecY and SecA but not on SecE or SecG, and it is not dependent on the signal recognition particle, although it can use the targeting pathway.
DsbA is translocated across the cytoplasmic membranes of Escherichia coil by a mechanism that differs from that of most secretory proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DsbA export is a special case of protein export in E. coli.

DsbA export is a peculiar event, which is not only dependent on the signal recognition particle pathway but also on an unknown route through the translocom, and that the translocon has a special mechanism for the export of this particular substrate.
the DsbA translocation is not a simple process, but is a unique one, requiring a specific export machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the general perception, the Sec translocon can be a highly selective channel for the export of proteins.
the SecY channel is a multifunctional protein complex that can be adapted to the specific needs of the various classes of secretory proteins.
DsbA, in contrast to most other secretory proteins, is translocated through the cytoplasmic SecY translocons in an ATP-independent manner.
